question: Question linked to image nº9 A 28-year-old woman who has been undergoing treatment for polycystic ovarian syndrome goes to the office for pregnancy control, referring to 10-week amenorrhea. Ultrasound revealed a single, live fetus with a cephalo-caudal length (CRL) of 57 mm, corresponding to 12 weeks. Point out the correct option:

options.opa: We must assume that the actual gestational age is 12 weeks, reassign a new FUR (Last Rule Date) or FPP (Probable Date of Delivery) and plan the rest of the pregnancy controls based on this gestational age.
options.opb: We will continue to consider that the actual gestational age is 10 weeks, since it coincides with the patient's FUR. We will plan the rest of the controls based on this gestational age, although we will record this discordance in the clinical history.
options.opc: Given this discrepancy, we will request a blood test to quantify the ß-HCG hormone and decide according to its levels what is the actual gestational age to be able to plan the rest of the pregnancy controls.
options.opd: We will request a new ultrasound control in 2 weeks to see the evolution and diagnose with more certainty the correct gestational age.
